quiz.question: Dafna Bank concludes on a Sunday morning that a payment is linked to a person suspected of supporting a terrorist organisation. What is the latest time limit under the QFIU's 2024 instructions?
options: Within 24 hours of that determination
Within three working days of that determination
Within five days of the QFIU's acknowledgement
By the end of the following month
quiz.explanation: Suspicions linked to a terrorist, a terrorist act or a terrorist organisation, or to high-risk crimes in the National Risk Assessment, must be reported within 24 hours. Three working days is the outer limit for other suspicions.

quiz.question: A customer starts a large transfer, then cancels it when asked to identify the beneficial owner. Nothing was processed. What applies?
options: Nothing, because only completed transactions are reportable
Only a note on the customer file is needed
The attempted transaction can and should be reported if it gives grounds for suspicion
The bank must close the account the same day
quiz.explanation: Law No. 20 of 2019 and the QFIU's instructions cover attempted transactions, including where a customer backs off when identification of parties is required. Closing the account is not required and could tip off the customer.

quiz.question: A relationship manager believes that asking more CDD questions will alert a customer that he is suspected. What does the law allow?
options: Continue the questions, because completing CDD always takes priority over any concern about the customer
Close the account quietly and keep no record
Ask the customer to visit the QFIU to explain
Stop pursuing the CDD and file an STR instead, with the MLRO recording the grounds
quiz.explanation: Article 22 of the law and section 20.2 of the Instructions let the bank file an STR instead of pursuing CDD when CDD would tip off the customer; the MLRO must keep records of the grounds, and the QFIU expects this to be stated in the narrative.

quiz.question: After filing an STR, Dafna decides for commercial reasons to end the customer relationship. What must it do?
options: Tell the customer the account is closed because of the STR
Ensure the exit does not tip off the customer and inform the QCB immediately
Delete the customer's records once the account is closed
Keep the account open, because exits are forbidden after an STR
quiz.explanation: The Instructions allow restricting or ending a relationship after an STR but require the bank to avoid tipping off and to inform the QCB immediately. Records must be kept, and must not be destroyed while the customer is under investigation without consulting the QFIU.

quiz.question: Which statement about protection for staff who report suspicions is correct under Law No. 20 of 2019?
options: Protection applies only if the suspicion is later proven in court
Good-faith reporters are protected even without knowing exactly what the underlying crime was
Protection covers only the MLRO, not other employees
Protection is lost if the report breaches a confidentiality clause in the customer's account terms and conditions
quiz.explanation: Article 22 protects institutions, directors, officers and employees from criminal and civil liability for breaching disclosure restrictions when reporting in good faith, even without knowing the precise predicate offence and whether or not it occurred.

quiz.question: The QFIU returns one of Dafna's STRs as incomplete. What happens if the bank does not send the extra information within the time allowed?
options: The QFIU may reject the STR and record the rejection for the supervisory authorities
The STR is automatically treated as complete
The bank may simply file the same STR again next month
The QFIU closes the case and deletes the data
quiz.explanation: The QFIU gives five days from its notice to provide information or a revised STR. If the bank fails, or the revised STR still falls short, it may reject the report, keep the data and report on rejected STRs to the supervisors.

quiz.question: A police request asks Dafna for statements on a customer. The analyst wants to file an STR that says only 'request received from the authorities'. Why is this weak under the QFIU's instructions?
options: Requests from authorities must never be mentioned in an STR
An STR can only be filed if no authority has asked about the customer, to avoid duplicating the request
STRs should present the bank's own analysis and conclusions, not merely cite a request
Police requests must be answered by the QFIU, not the bank
quiz.explanation: The QFIU says reporting entities should not limit their reasons to receiving a request from a competent authority; they should give an overall analysis of the customer's activity. Mentioning an investigation is allowed, using the authority and file references rather than officers' names.

quiz.question: A colleague in the trade finance team, not involved in the case, asks the MLRO's assistant whether a well-known client has been reported. What should happen?
options: The assistant can confirm it, because colleagues inside the bank are already bound by confidentiality
The colleague can be told if he promises to keep it confidential
The client's relationship manager decides who is told
Nothing is shared without the MLRO's consent, given only if it would not tip off
quiz.explanation: The QCB Instructions limit information on internal STRs to the board unless the MLRO consents, and the MLRO consents only if disclosure would not amount to tipping off and must record it. Being an employee is not a reason to know.

sessions.title: The Bank's Programme: Board, MLRO, Training, Records, Audit and Supervision
sessions.summary: Prepare for the QCB's review: the six key principles, board and senior management duties, the MLRO and Deputy MLRO, staff screening, the annual training programme under sections 21.2-21.3, ten-year record keeping, internal and external audit, and the supervisory measures the law allows.
objectives: Explain the six key principles and the board's specific AML/CFT responsibilities under the QCB Instructions
Describe the MLRO's eligibility, approval, independence, duties and annual report to the board
Apply the training, staff screening and record-keeping requirements, including the 10-year retention rules
Summarise the audit expectations, annual deadlines and supervisory measures that apply to banks

cards.title: The QCB letter
cards.setting: Board room, Dafna Bank head office, West Bay. 10:00 am.

lines.text: Good morning. The QCB's letter asks for our annual AML/CFT policy assessment, the MLRO's annual report and evidence of staff training. I want to know we are ready.
The policy assessment record is due to the QCB before the end of the first quarter, and the board must consider my annual report within four months of the year end.
Training is mostly fine, but Al Khor branch had staff changes. I'm not sure every new joiner's training record is on file.
And one of our directors has suggested outsourcing the MLRO role to a consultancy to save costs. Is that allowed?
Short answer: no. Long answer: that's what this final stage is about. The programme is only as strong as the evidence we can show.

cards.title: Six key principles in the QCB Instructions

scenes.heading: Board and top management
scenes.narration: The board approves AML/CFT policies, procedures, systems and controls; senior management makes sure they are implemented and meet the law and the Instructions.

scenes.heading: Risk-based approach
scenes.narration: Everything in the Instructions is applied through a risk-based approach, with effort matched to risk.

scenes.heading: Know your customer
scenes.narration: The bank must know each customer to the extent its risk profile requires.

scenes.heading: Effective reporting
scenes.narration: There must be effective internal and external reporting whenever money laundering or terrorist financing is known or suspected.

scenes.heading: Screening and training
scenes.narration: High standards when hiring, and an appropriate, ongoing AML/CFT training programme for officers and employees.

scenes.heading: Evidence of compliance
scenes.narration: The bank must be able to prove its compliance with documents. If it isn't recorded, it is hard to show it happened.

cards.title: Who carries AML/CFT responsibility at Dafna Bank
cards.caption: Outsourcing a function does not move responsibility: the bank and its board remain responsible for compliance.

items.label: Board of directors
items.detail: Overall responsibility for effective controls, approvals, training programme and a competent MLRO

items.label: Senior management
items.detail: Implements policies, procedures, systems and controls day to day

items.label: MLRO and Deputy MLRO
items.detail: Oversee the programme, decide on STRs, liaise with the QFIU and QCB, report to the board

items.label: Internal and external audit
items.detail: Independently test effectiveness and report gaps

items.label: Every officer and employee
items.detail: Apply CDD, monitor, report suspicion internally and avoid tipping off

cards.title: Who must do what
cards.prompt: Match each role with a duty the QCB Instructions give it.

pairs.right: Consider the MLRO's annual report within four months of the year end and approve action plans
Receive and assess internal STRs and decide whether to report to the QFIU
Act as MLRO during absences or vacancies so the function is never interrupted
Review the effectiveness of AML/CFT controls every year, including branches and subsidiaries
Verify compliance with the Instructions and inform the QCB immediately of major violations
Make internal STRs promptly and comply with the bank's AML/CFT procedures

cards.question: Which description fits the MLRO eligibility rules in the QCB Instructions?
options: Any compliance analyst, reporting to the head of retail and based anywhere in the group
Employed at management level, reporting directly to the board and resident in Qatar
An external consultant, reporting to the chief executive under a service contract
A board member, who reports to the QCB instead of the board
cards.explanation: Section 8.2 requires the MLRO to be at management level with sufficient seniority, knowledge, experience and authority, to report directly to the board and to be resident in Qatar. Section 8.1 also forbids outsourcing the MLRO position.

cards.title: Dafna Bank's AML/CFT calendar
cards.caption: Based on sections 6.4, 8.7, 9.1, 21.2 and 23.1 of the QCB AML/CFT Instructions.

items.label: Monitoring and screening
items.detail: Ongoing CDD reviews, real-time monitoring and list screening

items.label: Business risk assessment
items.detail: ML/TF risk assessment using the National Risk Assessment

items.label: Staff training
items.detail: Training for all staff, plus extra whenever needed

items.label: Policy assessment to QCB
items.detail: Record of the annual review and testing of policies and controls sent to the QCB

items.label: MLRO annual report
items.detail: Board considers it no later than four months after the fiscal year ends

items.label: Internal audit review
items.detail: Risk-based audit of AML/CFT effectiveness for branches and subsidiaries

cards.title: Training under sections 21.2 and 21.3
The training cycle
cards.prompt: Put Dafna Bank's AML/CFT training cycle in order.
steps: Review training needs, using STR analysis, audit findings and role changes
Design content for each group's role, level and risk exposure
Deliver training to all staff at least annually and whenever needed
Record who was trained, on what and when
Present the outcome of the training needs review to the board
Approve and carry out an action plan to fix any deficiencies

lines.text: Found the gap. Two new joiners at Al Khor did their AML/CFT training online, but the completion records never reached the training system.
The QCB will ask for evidence, and training records must be kept for 10 years.
Then we fix it properly: confirm completion, restore the records, and log the gap in my annual report as a control weakness.
What about the other records? Customer files, transactions, STR analysis?
Ten years is the rule of thumb, but the starting point changes. Let's sort them out.

cards.title: When does the 10-year clock start?
cards.prompt: Sort each record into the retention rule the QCB Instructions apply.
buckets: 10 years or until a judgment, if longer

items.text: Domestic and international transaction records
Records of a one-off transaction for a walk-in customer
KYC documents such as ID and passport copies of an account holder
Account files and business correspondence with the customer
Analysis of an unusual transaction that is in court proceedings
Records of a suspicious transaction under judicial review

cards.title: Outsource the MLRO?
cards.situation: To cut costs, a director proposes that a group consultancy in another country take over the MLRO role. A junior compliance analyst in Doha would 'handle the paperwork'. Hamad asks Noora for her view before the board meeting.

choices.text: Support it, as long as the consultancy is experienced
choices.outcome: This conflicts with the QCB Instructions: the MLRO position must not be outsourced, and the MLRO must be resident in Qatar, at management level and report directly to the board.

choices.text: Advise against it, explain the QCB rules and propose keeping an in-house MLRO and Deputy with adequate resources
choices.outcome: Right. The board must ensure a competent, independent, adequately resourced MLRO and a Deputy, and any appointment or removal needs QCB approval. Noora can suggest other savings, such as better monitoring tools.

choices.text: Accept it, but ask the QCB afterwards whether it minds
choices.outcome: Asking afterwards does not fix a breach. The MLRO's appointment and removal require QCB approval in advance, and outsourcing the role is not allowed at all.

cards.front: Who are higher-impact individuals?
cards.back: People with a role in preventing ML/TF, such as senior officials, the MLRO, the Deputy MLRO and anyone in a controlled function.

cards.front: What is checked before hiring?
cards.back: References, employment history and qualifications, criminal convictions or regulatory actions, and the accuracy of what was provided.

cards.front: Is screening one-off?
cards.back: No. Screening of higher-impact individuals must be continuous and regular, for example sanctions name checks and profile changes.

cards.front: What can the QCB do after a breach?
cards.back: Under the law: warnings, orders, regular reports, fines on the bank and managers, restrictions or removal of managers, and licence suspension or withdrawal.

cards.front: Can individuals be fined?
cards.back: Yes. The law allows financial penalties on directors, board members, executives and managers of supervised institutions.

cards.front: What if the QCB issues guidance?
cards.back: The MLRO brings it to the board; the bank records whether the board considered it, what it did and why.

cards.question: How long must Dafna Bank keep its AML/CFT training records under the QCB Instructions?
options: At least 5 years
Until the employee leaves the bank
Only until the next QCB inspection
At least 10 years
cards.explanation: Section 22.1 lists training records among the records that must be kept for 10 years, alongside transaction, account and STR-related records. Shorter or event-based periods do not meet the rule.

cards.title: Real case: how the QFIU raised report quality (QFIU, 2021-2022)
cards.body:
The QFIU's 2021-2022 annual report describes how it improved Qatar's reporting system.

- It set up a **Quality Control and Collection Department** to rate reports objectively, carry out preliminary analysis and contact reporting entities when reports **lacked information or grounds for suspicion**.
- In line with the law, its regulations and **QCB instructions**, it limited reporting to each entity's **registered reporting officers and deputies**, with a dedicated database of their details.
- It ran the **Forum of the Public-Private Dialogue** five times in 2021-2022 with supervisors and reporting entities.
- It reported contributing to the recovery of about **QR 1.02 billion**.

**Lessons for your bank:** the QFIU watches report quality and timeliness and shares its view with supervisors. Your MLRO registration, narratives and deadlines are part of how the QCB judges your programme.

cards.title: Getting inspection-ready
cards.body:
- **Evidence, not intentions.** Keep approved policies, risk assessments, board minutes and MLRO reports where you can find them.
- **Close the loop.** Each audit or training gap needs an owner, a date and proof it was fixed.
- **Check approvals.** MLRO and Deputy appointments need QCB approval, and changes must be reported to the QCB and the QFIU.
- **Test retrieval.** Can you rebuild a transaction from 2017 quickly? Records must be retrievable without undue delay.
- **Watch for change.** The law was amended in 2021; check official sources for later changes and new QCB circulars.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: The board approves and oversees the programme; senior management implements it; the bank and board stay responsible even when work is outsourced.
The MLRO is at management level, resident in Qatar, reports to the board, needs QCB approval and is never outsourced; a Deputy covers absences.
Train all staff at least annually and when needed, tailor training to roles and risk, review needs regularly and keep training records for 10 years.
Keep transaction, account, STR-related and wire records for at least 10 years, retrievable quickly enough to reconstruct transactions.
Annual risk assessment, policy assessment to the QCB before the end of Q1, MLRO report to the board within four months, and annual internal audit.

cards.prompt: If a QCB inspector asked you tomorrow for proof that you completed this year's AML/CFT training and know how to report a suspicion, what evidence could you show?

quiz.question: Which of these is one of the six key principles in the QCB AML/CFT Instructions?
options: Profit protection: controls must not reduce revenue
Customer anonymity: privacy overrides due diligence
Self-certification: customers confirm their own risk level
Evidence of compliance: the bank must be able to show documentary proof
quiz.explanation: The six principles are board and top management responsibility, the risk-based approach, know your customer, effective reporting, high-standard screening and training, and evidence of compliance. The other options contradict the Instructions.

quiz.question: Who must approve the appointment or removal of Dafna Bank's MLRO and Deputy MLRO?
options: The QFIU
The bank's external auditor
The QCB
The National AML/CFT Committee
quiz.explanation: Section 8.1 requires the bank to seek QCB approval when appointing or removing an MLRO or Deputy, and if either resigns. The QFIU registers approved officers but relies on the supervisor's approval.

quiz.question: Dafna's fiscal year ends on 31 December. By when must the board consider the MLRO's annual report?
options: No later than 31 January, one month after the year end
No later than 30 April, four months after the year end
No later than 31 December of the following year
Whenever the next QCB inspection is scheduled
quiz.explanation: Section 8.7 requires the board to consider the MLRO's annual report in a timely manner and no later than four months after the end of the fiscal year, and to approve an action plan if it shows deficiencies.

quiz.question: Which item must the MLRO's annual report to the board include under the QCB Instructions?
options: The number and types of internal STRs, and how many were passed to the QFIU, with reasons
The names of every customer reported to the QFIU during the year, together with their current account balances
A copy of every STR filed, attached in full
A list of employees who made internal STRs, for performance reviews
quiz.explanation: The report must cover numbers and types of internal STRs and those passed or not passed to the QFIU with reasons, among other items such as training and high-risk customer numbers. Naming customers or reporters widely would undermine confidentiality.

quiz.question: Under section 21.2, how often must Dafna Bank train all staff on AML/CFT?
options: Once at induction only
Every two years, aligned with policy updates
Only when the QCB issues a new circular
At least annually, and whenever necessary
quiz.explanation: Section 21.2 requires the ongoing training programme to be delivered at least annually for all staff and whenever necessary, for example after a change in law or policy. Induction-only or two-yearly training falls short.

quiz.question: The latest training needs review finds that branch staff struggle to recognise trade-based laundering. What must happen next under section 21.3?
options: The MLRO files an STR about the branch staff
The bank waits for the next annual training session to cover it, so that the training calendar is not disrupted
The board considers the review outcome and approves an action plan to fix the gap promptly
Branch staff are moved out of customer-facing roles
quiz.explanation: Section 21.3 requires regular reviews of training needs, board consideration of each outcome and a prompt, approved action plan when deficiencies are found. An STR is for suspicion about transactions, not training gaps.

quiz.question: A customer closed his account in 2020. How long must Dafna keep his KYC documents and account file?
options: At least 10 years from the date the account was opened
At least 10 years from the date the account was closed
At least 5 years from the last transaction
Until the customer asks for them to be deleted
quiz.explanation: Law No. 20 of 2019 and section 22.1 require account-related records to be kept at least 10 years after the relationship ends, so the clock starts at closure. Counting from opening could destroy records too early.

quiz.question: Records of an unusual transaction are linked to a court case expected to last beyond the normal retention period. How long must they be kept?
options: At least 10 years or until a final judgment or decision, whichever is longer
Exactly 10 years, then destroyed regardless of the case
Until the QFIU acknowledges the STR
Until the customer is notified of the outcome
quiz.explanation: Section 22.1 requires records of unusual and suspicious transactions to be kept for at least 10 years or until a judgment or final decision where there is judicial involvement, whichever is longer.

quiz.question: The external auditor finds that Dafna's sanctions screening has not run for three months. What do the QCB Instructions expect of the auditor?
options: Keep the finding confidential between the auditor and management until the screening system has been repaired
Fix the screening system on the bank's behalf
Report it in the management letter and inform the QCB immediately of the major violation
Inform the customers who were not screened
quiz.explanation: Section 23.1 requires the external auditor to verify the bank's compliance, include the results in the management letter and inform the QCB immediately of any major violation. Auditors do not run the bank's controls, and informing customers would be inappropriate.

quiz.question: When hiring a new Deputy MLRO, which screening step is required under section 21.1?
options: Check only the candidate's academic certificates
Seek and verify information on any criminal convictions or regulatory actions
Rely on the candidate's own signed declaration about his background, without any further verification
Screen once at hiring and never again
quiz.explanation: For higher-impact roles such as the Deputy MLRO, screening must confirm references, employment history and qualifications, and seek and verify information on convictions or regulatory actions, and it must continue regularly after hiring.

bank.question: Which instrument issued the Implementing Regulations of Law No. 20 of 2019?
options: QCB Circular No. 25 of 2022
Decree-Law No. 19 of 2021
Council of Ministers Decision No. 41 of 2019
Law No. 27 of 2019 on Combating Terrorism
bank.explanation: The Council of Ministers issued the Implementing Regulations by Decision No. 41 of 2019, which the QCB Instructions cite as part of their legal basis. Decree-Law No. 19 of 2021 amended the law itself.

bank.question: A Dafna customer receives rent from a flat bought with money he knows his brother embezzled. Which part of the money laundering offence most directly covers him?
options: Financing the travel of individuals for terrorist purposes
Acquiring, possessing or using funds known at receipt to be proceeds of crime
Failing to declare currency when crossing the border
Providing false information about a company's beneficial owner to a financial institution
bank.explanation: Article 2 covers acquiring, possessing or using funds known to be criminal proceeds when received, including income derived from them. The other options are separate offences that do not describe holding embezzled proceeds.

bank.question: Fraud is committed abroad and its proceeds are deposited in Qatar. When does it count as a predicate offence under Law No. 20 of 2019?
options: Only when a foreign court has already convicted the offender
Only when the proceeds exceed QR 50,000
Never, because only offences committed in Qatar qualify
When the conduct generates funds and is a crime both where it happened and in Qatar
bank.explanation: The law defines a predicate offence as any felony or misdemeanour that generates funds, whether committed inside or outside Qatar, provided it is punishable in both countries. No conviction or amount threshold is required.

bank.question: Investigators find that a charity volunteer sent lawful donations to an individual on a terrorist list, though no attack was planned. A colleague says this cannot be TF because no terrorist act was linked. What is the correct view?
options: It can be TF, because funding an individual terrorist is covered without a link to a specific act
The colleague is right, because TF always needs a planned attack
It can only be money laundering, because the funds were donations collected from members of the public
It is an offence only if the money was used within Qatar
bank.explanation: Article 3 covers funds provided to an individual terrorist or terrorist organisation even without a link to a specific act, from any source, and wherever the parties are. Lawful origin does not prevent TF.

bank.question: A person learns that a friend is laundering money through a car business and deliberately says nothing to the authorities. The friend is not a relative. What risk does he face under Law No. 20 of 2019?
options: None, because only banks have a duty to report
Only a supervisory warning from the QCB
Liability only if he also received some of the money, because silence alone is never a crime in Qatar
Criminal liability for failing to inform the authorities of an offence he knows about
bank.explanation: The law makes it an offence for a person who knows offences under the law have been or will be committed not to inform the competent authorities, with an exemption only for a spouse or relatives up to the second degree.

bank.question: Which pair correctly matches an authority with its role under Qatar's AML/CFT framework?
options: QFIU: licenses banks and approves their MLROs
Public Prosecution: issues the QCB AML/CFT Instructions and approves each bank's AML/CFT policy
NCTC: circulates terrorist designations that banks must screen against
QFCRA: receives STRs from onshore banks
bank.explanation: The NCTC circulates terrorist designation orders that the QCB Instructions require banks to screen against. The QCB licenses banks and approves MLROs, the QCB issues its own Instructions, and onshore STRs go to the QFIU.

bank.question: The QCB finds serious, repeated AML/CFT breaches at a bank. Which outcome is among the supervisory measures in Law No. 20 of 2019?
options: Imprisonment of the bank's directors by QCB order
Suspending or replacing managers and suspending or withdrawing the licence
Confiscation of customers' deposits by the QCB
Automatic transfer of the bank to the QFIU's control
bank.explanation: The law lets supervisors issue warnings and orders, impose fines on the institution and its managers, restrict or remove managers, appoint a supervisor and suspend or withdraw licences. Imprisonment and confiscation are court matters, not QCB measures.

bank.question: A Dafna director asks which laws the QCB applies when it sanctions AML/CFT breaches of its Instructions. What do the Instructions say?
options: Article 44 of Law No. 20 of 2019 and the relevant articles of the QCB Law
Only internal disciplinary rules of the bank
Only the penalties in the Penal Code for fraud
Only voluntary settlements agreed with the QFIU after it reviews the bank's reporting record
bank.explanation: Section 4 of the QCB Instructions says breaches are sanctioned under Article 44 of Law No. 20 of 2019 as well as articles of the QCB Law, and section 23.2 confirms sanctions follow the AML/CFT Law.

bank.question: Dafna plans to launch an app that lets new customers open accounts entirely online. When must the ML/TF risk of this channel be assessed?
options: Within a year of launch, at the next annual risk assessment
Only after the first suspicious case appears
Before the app is launched, with mitigating controls in place from day one
Never, because online channels are lower risk than branches
bank.explanation: Law No. 20 of 2019 requires risks of new products, practices and technologies to be assessed before use, and the QCB Instructions require interface risk to be assessed before introducing a new product or technology. Non-face-to-face business is an EDD category, not a low-risk one.

bank.question: During a QCB review, Dafna cannot explain how its business risk assessment used the National Risk Assessment. What do the QCB Instructions expect?
options: Nothing, because the National Risk Assessment is a confidential document used only by government bodies
The bank must adopt the National Risk Assessment word for word as its own
The QFIU must certify the bank's risk assessment instead
The bank must show how it considered the National Risk Assessment, or explain why not
bank.explanation: Section 10.6 requires a bank to demonstrate how it determined its risks and took the National Risk Assessment into account, and to give reasons if it failed to do so when the QCB requires. Copying it word for word would ignore the bank's own risks.

bank.question: A joint stock company applies for an account. One shareholder holds 12% and has no other control. Under the QCB Instructions, what must Dafna record about this shareholder?
options: Name and address, because shareholders above 10% of a joint stock company must be recorded
Nothing, because only owners of 20% or more are relevant
Full beneficial owner verification, because every shareholder is a beneficial owner
Only the shareholder's nationality
bank.explanation: For joint stock companies, identification data must include the names and addresses of shareholders above 10% of capital. The 20% test identifies beneficial owners who need verification, so a 12% holder is recorded but is not automatically a beneficial owner.

bank.question: A family trust has already fixed its beneficiaries: one receives 50%, two receive 20% each and one receives 10%. Whom must Dafna identify as beneficiaries under section 14.6?
options: Only the beneficiary receiving 50%
The beneficiaries receiving 50%, 20% and 20%
All four, including the one receiving 10%
None, because trusts are identified only through the trustee
bank.explanation: Where beneficiaries and their shares are already decided, the bank must identify each beneficiary entitled to at least 20% of the arrangement's funds. The 10% beneficiary falls below that threshold, though other parties such as the trustee must still be identified.

bank.question: Which situation allows Dafna to verify a customer's identity after the relationship has started, under section 14.9?
options: The customer is a PEP who is in a hurry
The customer refuses to provide documents now
Delay avoids interrupting normal business, risk is low and managed, and verification follows promptly
A branch target must be met before the quarter ends and the regional manager approves the delay in writing
bank.explanation: Later verification is allowed only when it is necessary to avoid interrupting normal business, ML/TF risk is low and effectively managed, CDD is completed as soon as practicable and policy conditions are met. PEPs require EDD before acceptance, and refusals or targets are not grounds.

bank.question: Dafna wants to apply simplified CDD to a customer it rates low risk, but the transactions raise a suspicion of fraud. What applies?
options: Simplified CDD continues, because the risk rating was approved
Simplified CDD is not allowed; full CDD applies and the suspicion must be escalated
Simplified CDD continues if the amount is below QR 50,000
The bank may choose either, provided it documents the choice
bank.explanation: Law No. 20 of 2019 says simplified measures are not acceptable whenever there is suspicion of ML/TF or specific higher-risk scenarios, and suspicion is itself a CDD trigger. A prior low-risk rating does not override that.

bank.question: A customer from a jurisdiction that FATF identifies as having strategic AML/CFT deficiencies wants to open a business account. What is the minimum Dafna must apply?
options: Enhanced CDD and enhanced monitoring, with proportionate countermeasures
Standard CDD, because FATF lists are advisory only
An automatic refusal of the account
A one-time check at onboarding, with no further monitoring once the account has been opened and approved
bank.explanation: Section 13.3 requires enhanced CDD and enhanced ongoing monitoring for transactions or relationships arising from such jurisdictions, with proportionate countermeasures. The rules do not require automatic refusal.

bank.question: When EDD is required, which measure appears in section 16.3 of the QCB Instructions?
options: Waiving source of funds checks if the customer is well known
Opening the account in a nominee name to protect privacy
Replacing senior management approval with a signed customer declaration about the source of funds
Making the first payment through an account at a bank supervised for AML/CFT
bank.explanation: Section 16.3 lists measures such as more information on the customer, purpose, source of wealth and funds, senior management approval, extra transaction controls and routing the first payment through a supervised bank account. Nominee or anonymous accounts are prohibited.

bank.question: Dafna's board adopts a policy of refusing all foreign PEPs automatically, without assessment. How does this sit with Qatar's rules?
options: It is required, because the law forbids foreign PEP relationships
The rules require PEP risk management and EDD, not a blanket ban
It is required only for PEPs from international organisations
It is prohibited, because the QCB requires banks to accept all PEPs who complete the account forms
bank.explanation: Law No. 20 of 2019 and the QCB Instructions require systems to identify PEPs and additional due diligence with board or delegated approval; they do not ban PEPs. A bank may set its risk appetite, but blanket refusal is not what the rules call for.

bank.question: Which capability must Dafna's ongoing monitoring system have under section 14.11?
options: The ability to review transactions in real time as they take place
The ability to approve all transactions without human review
The ability to delete alerts that are older than a year
The ability to share alerts with customers automatically
bank.explanation: Section 14.11 requires systems that flag transactions for further examination and can review transactions in real time. Deleting alerts or sharing them with customers would breach record-keeping and tipping-off rules.

bank.question: A customer makes several one-off cash transactions over two days that add up to QR 52,000. Staff believe he split them on purpose. Under section 14.12, what must Dafna do?
options: Refund the transactions and say nothing
Wait for a third day of activity to confirm the pattern
Make an STR, because it suspects the transactions were linked to avoid the QR 50,000 threshold
Ask the customer to sign a declaration that the transactions are unrelated and keep it on file for audit
bank.explanation: Section 14.12 requires an STR when the bank knows or suspects that linked one-off transactions are meant to circumvent the QR 50,000 CDD threshold. Asking for a declaration does not address the suspicion and could tip off.

bank.question: Dafna sends a domestic transfer of QR 2,500 to another bank in Doha, using only the names and account numbers of the parties. What condition makes this acceptable?
options: The customer signs a waiver of the information rules
The beneficiary bank confirms the payment within 24 hours and stores the customer's full details on its own system
The transfer is made on a weekday before noon
Full details can be given to the beneficiary bank, QCB or QFIU within three days, and to police at once
bank.explanation: For domestic transfers below QR 3,500, the reduced data set is allowed only if all originator and recipient information can be given within three days of a request to the beneficiary institution, the QCB or the QFIU, and immediately to law enforcement.

bank.question: Dafna is both the ordering and the beneficiary bank for a transfer between two of its customers in different countries. The combined information looks suspicious. What must it do?
options: Report only in the country where the originator is located
Report nothing, because the money never left the bank
Consider both sides and, if suspicious, report in each affected country and share information with their FIUs
Ask each branch to decide separately, without sharing information, because customer data cannot cross borders under any rule
bank.explanation: Law No. 20 of 2019 and section 18 of the Instructions require a bank controlling both sides of a transfer to take all information into account and, where suspicious, report in every affected country and make the information available to those FIUs.

bank.question: Samuel's team sends payments for one corporate customer in a batch file to recipients abroad. One payment in the batch is a large, unusual transfer. What does section 18 require?
options: Batching is fine as long as the file contains the originator's account number for each individual payment
Non-routine transfers must not be batched, so the unusual payment goes separately
Batching is required for all transfers of the same customer
The unusual payment may be batched if the total is below QR 50,000
bank.explanation: Batch files are allowed when they carry full, traceable originator and recipient information, but the ordering institution must make sure non-routine transfers are not batched, to avoid increased ML/TF risk.

bank.question: Before opening a correspondent relationship, what must Dafna check about the respondent under section 11.4?
options: Only the respondent's credit rating and profitability
Only whether the respondent uses the same core banking software
Only whether the respondent's customers are all residents of Qatar, because foreign customers are not allowed to use the account
Any ML/TF investigations or proceedings against it, and whether its leaders are on sanctions lists
bank.explanation: Section 11.4 requires checks on reputation, supervision, ownership, management, business, AML/CFT controls, any ML/TF investigations or proceedings, financial position and whether board members and executives are on international sanctions lists.

bank.question: A foreign bank approaches Dafna. It is licensed in a small territory but has no staff or management there and belongs to no supervised group. What must Dafna do?
options: Refuse the relationship and make an STR to the QFIU
Open the relationship with enhanced monitoring
Ask the QCB for permission to open the account
Open the account only for trade finance
bank.explanation: This is a shell bank. Relationships with shell banks are prohibited, and section 11.5 requires an STR to the QFIU when a bank is approached by a shell bank or an institution it suspects is one.

bank.question: Screening shows a possible match between an existing customer and a name on a UN Security Council list. Further checks confirm it is the same person. Which statement is correct?
options: Existing customers are exempt, because screening applies only at onboarding
The bank may continue until the customer's next periodic review
Screening is ongoing, so a confirmed match must be acted on within 24 hours even for old customers
Only new transactions need to stop, while existing balances may still be withdrawn by the customer as normal
bank.explanation: Section 10.4 requires screening from the outset and on an ongoing basis. On a match, the bank must not continue the relationship or carry out any transaction, immediately and within 24 hours, file an STR and inform the QCB within 24 hours.

bank.question: Which law provides the wider legal basis for Qatar's targeted financial sanctions against designated terrorists, alongside Law No. 20 of 2019?
options: Law No. 13 of 2016 on personal data privacy
Law No. 27 of 2019 on Combating Terrorism
Law No. 8 of 2012 on the Qatar Financial Markets Authority
Law No. 11 of 2015 on commercial companies
bank.explanation: Law No. 20 of 2019 defines targeted financial sanctions by reference to persons listed under the Combating Terrorism Law, Law No. 27 of 2019, which the QFIU lists with a 2020 implementing decision. The other laws do not set the TFS regime.

bank.question: Under section 19.5 of the QCB Instructions, which situation still requires an STR to the QFIU?
options: The bank has only a general dislike of the customer's industry
The customer's transactions are large but fully explained by verified business
A rival bank told Dafna informally that it had closed the customer's account, with no other information
The customer's attempted laundering failed and the bank has since ended the relationship
bank.explanation: STRs must be made even if no transaction happened, no relationship was formed, the relationship has ended or the attempt failed. Dislike of an industry, explained activity or an unsupported rumour are not grounds for suspicion by themselves.

bank.question: Dafna files an STR about a transfer the customer has asked for but which has not yet been sent. What else must the bank do under the QCB Instructions?
options: Inform the QCB and make sure the transaction does not proceed without consulting the QFIU
Send the transfer immediately so the customer is not alerted
Tell the customer the transfer is under review by the QFIU
Cancel the STR, because the transaction has not happened yet
bank.explanation: Section 19.5 says related future or proposed transactions must not proceed without consulting the QFIU, and section 19.6 requires the bank to inform the QCB when it reports a proposed transaction. Telling the customer would be tipping off.

bank.question: Dafna is not yet connected to the QFIU's E-STR system and has an urgent case. How should the report be submitted under the QFIU's 2024 instructions?
options: By ordinary email from the branch that detected the activity, copying the MLRO and the branch manager for speed
Through the QCB's customer complaints portal
On the signed paper STR form in a sealed envelope to the QFIU, and contact the QFIU about the urgency
By telephone only, with no written report
bank.explanation: Entities not connected to E-STR, or in urgent cases, file the approved paper form, signed by the MLRO or Deputy, in a sealed envelope at the QFIU; urgent cases should also be flagged by contacting the QFIU's Analysis Department.

bank.question: An analyst drafting an STR writes 'cust triggered TM-07 and KYC-R3, see CRM note'. Which QFIU expectation does this break?
options: Avoid acronyms and internal jargon that the QFIU may misread
Always write STRs in Arabic only
Never mention transaction monitoring systems
Keep narratives under 50 words
bank.explanation: The QFIU's instructions ask reporting entities to avoid acronyms and jargon that may be misunderstood and to explain the reasons for suspicion in a clear narrative. Mentioning monitoring alerts is fine if explained.

bank.question: Dafna files a second STR about a customer it reported last year. What should the new report contain under the QFIU's instructions?
options: Only the new transactions, because the QFIU already holds the first report and will link the two itself
The earlier reference and date, a restatement of the earlier grounds and the new reasons
Only the earlier reference number, with no further narrative
A request that the QFIU merge the reports without any new detail
bank.explanation: For a linked STR, the bank must indicate the earlier reference number and date and restate the earlier elements of suspicion, even with the reference number included, plus the new grounds.

bank.question: Under the QFIU's 2024 instructions, how is the reporting deadline counted when suspicion is determined just before a public holiday?
options: All calendar days count, including weekends and holidays
Only Fridays are excluded, Saturdays count
The deadline pauses until the MLRO returns from leave
Fridays, Saturdays and official national holidays are excluded from the working days counted
bank.explanation: The QFIU excludes the weekend, Friday and Saturday, official regular national holidays and specially declared national holidays when counting reporting periods. The MLRO's absence is covered by the Deputy MLRO, not by pausing deadlines.

bank.question: Which statement about suspicion matches the QFIU's 2024 instructions?
options: One red flag is always enough to file an STR
Suspicion must be based mainly on the customer's nationality, age and occupation, which the QFIU uses to rank reports
Suspicion usually rests on several factors about behaviour, not one factor or who the person is
Suspicion requires proof that a crime was committed
bank.explanation: The QFIU explains that suspicion combines objective and subjective criteria, that one factor alone is usually insufficient and that suspicion concerns behaviour, not people. Proof of a crime is not required; reasonable grounds suffice.

bank.question: A branch manager wants to share details of an internal STR with the relationship manager 'so he can keep an eye on the customer'. What do the QCB Instructions require?
options: Details go beyond the board only with the MLRO's consent, which the MLRO records
Branch managers may share STR details with any staff in their branch
The relationship manager must always be told, because he owns the customer and must monitor the account
STR details may be shared if the customer is a high-value client
bank.explanation: Section 20.3 restricts information on internal STRs to the board unless the MLRO consents, which the MLRO may do only if disclosure will not tip off, and must record. Branch hierarchy or client value does not change this.

bank.question: In a smaller bank, the board wants the MLRO also to act as compliance officer. When do the QCB Instructions allow this?
options: Always, because the two roles are identical
When size and spread are limited and the combination creates no conflict of interest
Never, because the MLRO must have no other duties
Only if the MLRO also heads a business line, so that compliance decisions stay close to the customers
bank.explanation: Section 8.1 allows the MLRO role to be combined with similar functions such as compliance when size and spread are limited and a full-time MLRO is not needed, but not with functions that create a conflict of interest, such as running a business line.

bank.question: Dafna's MLRO resigns unexpectedly. What must the board do under the QCB Instructions?
options: Leave the post empty until the next financial year
Ask the external auditor to file STRs until a new MLRO starts
Appoint the head of sales immediately without informing the QCB, since the role must never be vacant
The Deputy MLRO acts meanwhile, and a replacement is appointed after QCB approval
bank.explanation: The board must ensure the MLRO position is never vacant; the Deputy acts as MLRO during absences and vacancies, and a replacement is appointed after QCB approval. Auditors do not file the bank's STRs.

bank.question: When deciding what training each group needs, which factor must Dafna consider under section 21.2(4)?
options: The training budget of competitor banks
Employees' personal preferences for online or classroom formats only
Any analysis of STRs showing where training needs to improve
Whether the QCB has recently fined another bank
bank.explanation: Section 21.2(4) lists needs, experience, skills, functions, roles and levels, supervision or independence, access to information, bank size and risk, training needs reviews and analysis of STRs. Competitor budgets and other banks' fines are not on the list.

bank.question: Which topic must Dafna's annual AML/CFT training cover under section 21.2(2)?
options: The bank's internal STR procedures and how to report effectively to the MLRO
Techniques for negotiating higher fees with corporate clients
How to appeal a QCB penalty in court
The bank's marketing strategy for the coming year
bank.explanation: Training must cover legal duties, staff roles and liability, ML/TF threats, methods and trends with product vulnerabilities and recognising suspicious transactions, and the internal STR procedures. The other topics are unrelated to AML/CFT.

bank.question: By when must Dafna send the QCB the record of its annual assessment of AML/CFT policies, procedures, systems and controls?
options: Within one week of the fiscal year end
Before the end of the first quarter of the following year
Only when the QCB asks during an inspection
At the end of the following year
bank.explanation: Section 6.4 requires an annual assessment of the adequacy and effectiveness of AML/CFT policies and controls, a record of the results and a copy to the QCB before the end of the first quarter of the following year.

bank.question: A QCB inspector asks Dafna to reconstruct a 2018 international transfer quickly. What do Law No. 20 of 2019 and the Instructions require of the records?
options: They may be summarised after five years, keeping only totals
They need only show the customer's name and the date
They can be destroyed once the customer's account is closed, provided the closure letter is kept on file
Kept at least 10 years and detailed enough to rebuild each transaction without undue delay
bank.explanation: Transaction records must be kept for at least 10 years after the transaction, be retrievable without undue delay and be sufficient to reconstruct individual transactions, for example as evidence in prosecutions.

bank.question: Dafna's internal audit plans to review AML/CFT controls only at head office this year. What do the QCB Instructions require?
options: A review every three years, covering head office only
No review, because the external auditor already covers AML/CFT controls in its annual management letter
A review only of branches that filed STRs during the year
A yearly review covering branches and subsidiaries in and outside Qatar, under a risk-based plan
bank.explanation: Section 23.1 requires internal audit to review the effectiveness of AML/CFT procedures and controls every year for branches and subsidiaries inside and outside Qatar, under an annual risk-based audit plan. External audit has its own separate role.

bank.question: A Dafna subsidiary abroad says local law stops it from applying one of the QCB's AML/CFT requirements. What must Dafna do?
options: Inform the QCB immediately and apply additional measures to manage the risk
Ignore the requirement, because foreign law always prevails
Close the subsidiary within 24 hours
Ask the QFIU to grant a written exemption
bank.explanation: Section 6.6 requires the bank to inform the QCB immediately and apply additional risk measures; if the QCB is not satisfied it can direct the bank, for example to suspend transactions. The QFIU does not grant exemptions.
